[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-7f1173838e]
Finding: The topic has no opening review of the algebraic rearrangement and signed numerical substitution used directly in its worked examples.
Breakdown: The examples require students to isolate a variable, divide every term by a coefficient, reverse every sign when multiplying an equation by -1, and evaluate an expression at a negative value. These substantial prior skills must be recalled while students learn the meanings and uses of line equations.
Checked: Searched all supplied teaching preceding these examples. The p3 and p4 identification questions rehearse interpreting and inserting coefficients, rather than equation manipulation or signed numerical evaluation. The examples demonstrate the combined applications but there is no opening review. No preceding topic is supplied or omitted: teachingComplete is true.

Proposed repair (add-review): Before p3-gradient-intercept-definition, add: (a) Make y the subject: y-6=2x. (b) Make y the subject: 3y+12-2x=0. (c) Multiply every term of -4x+y+3=0 by -1. Finding: The topic has no opening review of bracket expansion, although its introductory worked examples use both positive and negative multipliers.
